topStories.headline: Developer Files Permits for 40-Story Apartment Tower on Mid-Market Parking Lot
topStories.dek: A Chicago-based firm has filed initial permits for a 433-foot, 288-unit skyscraper at 38 8th Street that would replace a surface parking lot steps from Civic Center.
topStories.body:
Initial permits have been filed for a potential 40-story mixed-use skyscraper at 38 8th Street in San Francisco's Mid-Market District. The high-rise proposal, reported this week by SF YIMBY and Bisnow, would replace a surface parking lot at the corner of 8th Street and Stevenson with nearly 300 apartments directly across from the Civic Center neighborhood.

Manna Capital is the project developer, filing on behalf of property owner Aslanian 2006 Revocable Trust of Napa County. The 433-foot-tall structure is expected to yield around 303,500 square feet, including 231,550 square feet of housing across 288 units and 37,250 square feet for a six-level podium garage. Of those total units, 38 would be officially designated as affordable housing for lower-income households.

The development team invoked California Senate Bill 330 and the State Density Bonus law — tools that can freeze local zoning rules, cap public hearings at five, and expedite permitting. Handel Architects is responsible for the design, with renderings showing a glassy tower defined by sawtooth bay windows and bold horizontal lines dividing the residential floors into four sections.

The proposal arrives as San Francisco's multifamily market tightens sharply. Downtown occupancy reached 97.4 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE, with average rents per unit rising 17.1 percent year-over-year. If approved and built, the skyscraper would be one of the tallest structures in Mid-Market and could inject significant residential density into a corridor that city leaders have long struggled to revitalize.

topStories.headline: SFJAZZ Launches 'Forward Motion' Season With Over 300 Shows; Christian McBride Opens September 10
topStories.dek: The nonprofit jazz presenter's 2026–27 season, led by new Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard, opens this fall at 201 Franklin Street with jazz legends and rising stars.
topStories.body:
SFJAZZ has launched its 2026–27 season, titled Forward Motion, marking a new chapter under Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard and CEO Gabrielle Armand. Across nine months and over 300 shows, programming at the SFJAZZ Center — on the corner of Franklin and Fell Streets, a block from Civic Center — spans jazz royalty to today's most innovative voices.

The season features centennial celebrations of Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Antonio Carlos Jobim, and Ray Brown, alongside performances by Ron Carter, Dianne Reeves, and Branford Marsalis. Rising stars including Isaiah Collier, Gabrielle Cavassa, Julian Lage, and Cécile McLorin Salvant round out a deep roster. The season opens locally with acclaimed bassist and bandleader Christian McBride at the Miner Auditorium on September 10 and 11.

Founded in 1983 as a two-day festival, SFJAZZ now serves more than a quarter of a million fans and students annually, making it the largest nonprofit jazz presenter in the world. The SFJAZZ Center, opened in 2013, is recognized as the first free-standing building in America built specifically for jazz performance and education. New flexible ticket packages for the full season are available at sfjazz.org.

topStories.headline: San Francisco Opera Opens 104th Season With Verdi's 'Simon Boccanegra' at September 12 Gala
topStories.dek: Opera Ball returns to City Hall and the War Memorial Opera House, with Music Director Eun Sun Kim and baritone Amartuvshin Enkhbat headlining the 2026–27 season opener.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Opera and San Francisco Opera Guild will open the Company's 104th season on Saturday, September 12, 2026, with Opera Ball — one of the city's grandest annual cultural evenings. The night begins with a cocktail reception and dinner beneath the City Hall rotunda, then moves across Van Ness Avenue to the War Memorial Opera House for the 8 p.m. opening performance of Giuseppe Verdi's Simon Boccanegra.

Music Director Eun Sun Kim conducts the San Francisco Opera Orchestra, Chorus, and a cast of top international artists. Mongolian baritone Amartuvshin Enkhbat returns for his third consecutive season-opening appearance, this time in his role debut as the title character; Italian soprano Eleonora Buratto joins the cast as well. After the curtain falls, guests return to City Hall for an after-party with DJ heyLove and live music from The Cosmo Alleycats and Big Crush.

Opera Ball is co-chaired by Sydney Leung and Jennifer Walske; proceeds support San Francisco Opera and the Opera Guild's artistic and education programming. The 2026–27 season continues through spring at the War Memorial, 301 Van Ness Avenue, at the heart of the Civic Center arts campus. Table and ticket packages are available through the San Francisco Opera development office at events@sfopera.com.

moreNews.headline: Tenderloin Museum Carrying Two Fundraisers as Flood-Related Closure Stretches On
moreNews.body: The Tenderloin Museum's summer closure — caused by water damage originating from the adjacent Cadillac Hotel in late June — is expected to last longer than initially hoped, with organizers now seeking $150,000 to reopen safely. Separately, a pre-existing expansion campaign aims to raise $50,000 by December 31 to build out a new 6,850-square-foot space that would triple the museum's footprint into rooms once occupied by Newman's Gym from the 1920s to the 1980s, where Muhammad Ali, Jack Dempsey, George Foreman, and Sugar Ray Robinson all trained or competed. Donors can direct contributions to either the flood-repair fund or the expansion campaign at tenderloinmuseum.org/donate.

moreNews.headline: Larkin Street Revival Showing Early Gains, but Drug Activity Remains a Threat to Progress
moreNews.body: The $5 million Larkin Street Revival Project — funded by Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen and managed by the Tenderloin Community Benefit District — has already improved conditions along the Larkin corridor between Golden Gate and Turk, according to Beyond Chron editor Randy Shaw. Decorative laser-cut security gates have been installed at roughly 20 businesses, and plans to activate the Eddy Street entrance to Little Saigon are in place. New bar Reggie & Maude's, from the owners of Outta Sight Pizza, is set to open at Larkin and Turk, filling a gap left by the closure of longtime anchor Turtle Tower. Shaw cautioned that persistent drug activity between O'Farrell and Geary still threatens to blunt the revival's impact in what he has called a make-or-break year for the neighborhood.

moreNews.headline: Phoenix Hotel Survives Closure Scare, Now Operating Under New Ownership
moreNews.body: The iconic Phoenix Hotel at 601 Eddy Street — which had announced it would close January 1, 2026, following a farewell New Year's Eve party — never actually shuttered. A new operator, local hotelier Binoy Patel, took over from the founding partnership led by Chip Conley and kept the staff largely intact. The property's landowner, James Beard Award-winning pastry chef Michel Suas, acquired the hotel's assets in early 2026. Patel told the San Francisco Chronicle he intends to preserve the hotel's signature pool parties, DJ nights, and the Celebrity Pool Toss. The hotel is currently open and accepting bookings at its longstanding Tenderloin address.

moreNews.headline: 40-Story Mid-Market Tower Sparks Debate Over Density, Affordability, and Parking
moreNews.body: The filing of permits for a 433-foot residential tower at 38 8th Street has prompted debate among urban observers. Proponents note the site — a surface parking lot near a Muni Metro station — is exactly where density belongs, pointing to surging rents as evidence of unmet housing demand. Skeptics have raised concerns about the six-story parking podium in the design and questioned whether market-rate rents at this price point serve the area's existing community. Developer Manna Capital invoked SB 330 and the State Density Bonus law to expedite approvals; the proposal designates 38 of the 288 units as affordable housing.
